summary: Weekly POC sync focused on why TTFT increased after switching to int8 kernels during the pilot. Team identified two contributing patterns: microburst prefill mismatch (cold key-value cache) and batching shaping that causes longer prefill latencies for short sequences. Action items: run an extended microburst test, SE to produce kernel timings, and update SOW for potential dedicated pilot capacity.
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-01-14 16:00 PST
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Luca Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Orchid Head of ML), Sam Ortiz (Orchid Infra), Jordan Lee (Orchid SRE), Ethan Morales (Redwood CSM), Tanya B. (Product)

[00:00] Maria Chen: okay everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to focus today's sync on the TTFT bump you folks saw after the int8 rollout, and the microburst behavior we saw in staging. quick status, priya?
[00:22] Priya Nair: thanks Maria. yes, last week we flipped to the int8 profile that's been suggested, and overall tokens/sec improved but TTFT — time to first token — spiked on short chat turns, like 8 to 20 tokens. p95 went up from about 120ms to 240ms. p99 is worse. we also observed weird streaming stalls during microbursts.
[00:47] Luca Patel: mmh, ok. do you have the sequence length histogram? is it more short turns than we expected? often quant profiles assume longer prefill amortization.
[01:05] Sam Ortiz: we do. attaching the bucketed distribution in the sheet you shared. it's 60% under 30 tokens, so a lot of short calls. also some requests have early function calls so the effective generation is 6-10 tokens.
[01:25] Jordan Lee: we noticed that when a microburst arrives (many concurrent short requests) the first byte latency for each new connection spikes — looks like the KV cache isn't warm and batch shaping merges lots of small requests into larger prefill paths, which paradoxically increases time-to-first.
[01:47] Luca Patel: yeah that's pretty classic. int8 kernels can have slightly different startup costs and memory paths. also the runtime's continuous batching can create a longer prefill if it waits for tokens to fill a batch. we have two levers: aggressive early-flush for short sequences and a separate small-batch fastpath kernel.
[02:10] Priya Nair: that would be ideal. our success criteria is sub-150ms p95 for short-chat. we can trade a small throughput loss for that SLA.
[02:25] Maria Chen: noted. Luca, can you summarize the kernel timing you measured?
[02:33] Luca Patel: sure. quick summary — these are rough: fp16 warm prefill 35-45ms, int8 warm prefill 28-40ms (better), but cold prefill with int8 jumps to 120-160ms because of an extra quant TLB/permute step on our current kernel path. the custom cuda kernel we've got reduces that cold step to ~60ms. also streaming code-paths introduce an extra 10-30ms in our current build because buffer assembly is serialized in one thread.
[03:02] Priya Nair: so int8 is faster when warm, but cold microbursts expose a penalty.
[03:12] Luca Patel: exactly. plus sequence length shaping means we sometimes treat a short request as a long prefill because the batch sampler expects longer context. we can implement a short-turn heuristic: if prompt tokens < 40 and expected gen < 32, route to fastpath.
[03:34] Sam Ortiz: can Redwood do routing by policy in the pilot? we can try that. also question on KV cache: is the cache per model instance, or shared across pool? because our bursts target 10 tenants simultaneously.
[03:52] Maria Chen: in the current pilot config the KV cache is per GPU worker, so cross-tenant bursts hit different caches. we can discuss cache warming strategies: prefix caching or prefetching popular prefixes during bursts.
[04:12] Jordan Lee: any quick wins? we need something for next week to meet internal deadlines.
[04:18] Luca Patel: quick win #1: enable short-turn fastpath and a lower batching window (drop wait from 8ms to 2ms) for sequences under 40 tokens. quick win #2: implement a short prefilling omit — don't do big context prefill for short sequences. quick win #3: server-side KV warmup for top 20 prompts.
[04:42] Priya Nair: awesome. what about streaming stalls?
[04:46] Luca Patel: streaming stalls often come from the single-threaded buffer assembly. we can change to lock-free ring buffer or use double-buffering to overlap assembly with kernel execution. that is more involved (SE work) but gives a steady reduction of 15-25ms in our tests.
[05:08] Tanya B.: are there security or compliance implications for aggressive caching? data residency?
[05:14] Maria Chen: good point. caching can respect tenant isolation: cache keys are namespaced by account and region. if you need no cache for some tenants, we can make that a policy. we also have audit logging hooks and can exclude PII from cache.
[05:33] Sam Ortiz: ok send us the patch notes on that.
[05:37] Ethan Morales: i'll include the security note in the follow-up.
[05:42] [10:00 marker missing — transcript jumps slightly here]
[06:10] Priya Nair: Luca, you mentioned a custom kernel that helps cold int8. what is the risk level for deploying that in staging?
[06:20] Luca Patel: low-medium. the kernel is a small change to permute+quant path; unit tests pass. we need a staging canary (10% traffic) to watch for regs. we can package it as a separate model variant, so fallback is easy.
[06:37] Maria Chen: can you prepare the canary patch and a runbook?
[06:41] Luca Patel: yes. I'll prepare detailed microbench results and the canary config. link to bench sheet: https://redwood.internal/pilot/orchid/microbench-jan14 (note: internal link)
[07:00] Sam Ortiz: on the 72-hour microburst run — we'll run in eu-west with 50 concurrent tenants, bursts every 7 minutes, with 60% short-turn mix. We'll attach traces to the sheet.
[07:16] Jordan Lee: will you include kernel traces (cuda NVTX) so we can see where time goes?
[07:21] Luca Patel: yes, we'll add NVTX and runtime-level timings. also include per-token p50/p95 and TTFT.
[07:32] Priya Nair: how much ops time to set the fastpath? is this flagged as a config toggle or code change?
[07:40] Luca Patel: shortpath toggle is config-first: we already support routing by policy (latency vs cost). enabling new routing profile is a config change; the buffer changes are code. So quick wins can be turned on in hours via config.
[07:58] Maria Chen: great. can we outline the cost tradeoffs? Priya asked for SLA and is willing to trade some throughput.
[08:06] Luca Patel: if you prioritize latency for short-turns we'll reduce batching headroom. roughly ballpark: for short-heavy workloads you might see 5-12% higher per-token cost but p95 improves by 40-60ms. We can quantify after microbench.
[08:26] Tanya B: also want to mention tool-calls: some of our prompts trigger function calls which increase prefill because tool metadata is big. can we compress tool payload or treat function calls as separate early-flush triggers?
[08:40] Luca Patel: yes, treat function calls as early-flush if payload exceeds X bytes. small change.
[08:48] Priya Nair: timeline. when can we expect the kernel CSV and config toggle?
[08:52] Luca Patel: kernel CSV by Monday 2026-01-18, fastpath config built and tested for canary by Wednesday 2026-01-21.
[09:00] Maria Chen: Maria to send SOW? (laugh)
[09:02] Maria Chen: yes, i'll update the pilot SOW with dedicated pool pricing and margin scenario, and include a clause for canary rollouts and rollback. expect that by 2026-01-20.
[09:14] Sam Ortiz: last question: fallback model. if the custom int8 causes issues can we fallback to fp16 automatically?
[09:20] Luca Patel: yes, the smart routing can fallback to a compatible fp16 variant and can do per-request retries. cost will go up but latency reliability will stay.
[09:34] Priya Nair: ok good. that answers most of our concerns.
[09:40] Maria Chen: recap quick: Redwood will share kernel timings and microbench CSV (Luca), will prepare short-turn fastpath toggle and canary plan, Maria will send SOW and pricing, Orchid will run 72-hour microburst and attach NVTX traces. action items captured.
[09:58] Ethan Morales: i'll include meeting notes and security considerations in the follow-up email plus link to the bench sheet.
[10:08] Maria Chen: thanks everyone. next sync scheduled provisional for 2026-01-22 to review microburst results.
[10:15] Priya Nair: thanks all.

Notes / artifacts referenced:
- microbench CSV + NVTX traces (to be uploaded)
- pilot config: 'shortpath-latency-first' (config toggle)
